The app tells you \"you\'ve done more than your share\" when you\'ve done at least X%% more than your target ratio. At 30%% (default) with a 50/50 ratio, the app congratulates you when you\'ve done 65%% of the work or more. At 0%%, the app congratulates as soon as you exceed your ratio. At 100%%, never (unless you do everything).

Your affinity is your personal preference for this task (from 1 = I hate it to 10 = I love it). It personalises YOUR suggestions, but doesn\'t affect others\' suggestions. Nobody can ask you to re-vote — it\'s your feeling.

Effort is the average time a task takes, voted on by each member of the household. It\'s used to compute the points earned when the task is validated — these feed the fair-share split between you and the household\'s overall backlog. The more votes, the more accurate. You can adjust your vote or ask another member to re-vote.

Effort is the average time a task takes, voted on by each member of the household. It helps better estimate the required time and prioritise between short and long tasks. The more votes, the more accurate. You can adjust your vote or ask another member to re-vote.
The displayed frequency is the average of votes from each household member. The more votes, the more representative. You can adjust your vote or ask another member to re-vote.

Tolerance doesn't change the displayed state of a task (green / orange / red) nor when it becomes overdue. It only affects the priority of the “most urgent” selector on the home page:

• STRICT: shown first as soon as it's overdue.
• NORMAL: shown if no strict task is overdue.
• LOOSE: shown last, when no other task is overdue.

To make a task turn red sooner, shorten its recurrence interval — not its tolerance.
